title: Chat statistics: top senders, daily counts, active chats
problem: This is the written SQL task from your assessment, made concrete. stats.py has three empty queries over the sample messages: the top senders of a chat within a time range, message counts per day, and per-chat activity since a moment. Write them with GROUP BY, HAVING, ORDER BY, LIMIT and a correct date range.
requirements: Edit only stats.py; use the named placeholders listed in each comment
TOP_SENDERS: (sender_id, messages) for one chat, only messages with start <= sent_at < end, blank bodies (spaces only) not counted, most messages first, ties by lower sender_id, at most :n rows
DAILY_COUNTS: (day, messages) per calendar day for one chat, all messages counted, only days with at least :min_messages, ordered by day; day is text like '2026-11-02'
ACTIVE_CHATS: (chat_id, senders, messages) for messages with sent_at >= :since; senders counts different people; most senders first, ties by lower chat_id
Every multi-row result has a fully defined order
contract: Each constant is one SELECT as a str, run with a dict of parameters: TOP_SENDERS {chat_id, start, end, n}; DAILY_COUNTS {chat_id, min_messages}; ACTIVE_CHATS {since}
edgeCases: A message whose body is only spaces (message 7) is not counted by TOP_SENDERS
A message sent exactly at start is included; one sent exactly at end is excluded
Two senders with the same count (tie-break by sender_id)
A range with no messages returns an empty list
A chat with one message from one sender counts as 1 sender, not 0
The same sender writing several messages counts once in senders
hints: Conceptual: decide which conditions are about single rows (WHERE, before grouping) and which are about whole groups (HAVING, after counting). Then: GROUP BY the thing you report one row per, ORDER BY, LIMIT.

Specific: the time range is two comparisons, >= :start and < :end, not BETWEEN. Blank means trim(body) is the empty string. Group by calendar day with date(sent_at). 'Different people' is count(DISTINCT sender_id).

Implementation: TOP_SENDERS is SELECT sender_id, count(*) AS messages FROM messages WHERE <chat, range, not blank> GROUP BY sender_id ORDER BY messages DESC, sender_id LIMIT :n. DAILY_COUNTS needs HAVING count(*) >= :min_messages.
evaluation: Row conditions are in WHERE, group conditions in HAVING
The time range is half-open (>= start, < end)
No bare columns: every selected column is grouped or aggregated
